business_problem: Mercari needed real-time change data capture across rapidly growing microservices and databases because batch updates every 10 minutes were too slow for fraud prevention, marketing incentives, and broader business operations.
solution_summary: Mercari adopted Confluent Cloud as the managed event backbone for its CDC architecture after deciding that operating Apache Kafka in house would consume scarce specialist capacity. Product and service teams already relied on Kubernetes-based microservices and BigQuery warehousing, so the data platform team used Confluent to capture changes from multiple databases in real time and stream them into downstream fraud, analytics, and marketing workflows. Schema Registry and the managed Kafka environment reduced the burden of standing up clusters, rebuilding them, and governing interfaces, while the team's CDC pipelines made it possible to replace ten-minute batch retrieval with continuous event delivery. That foundation now supports real-time fraud detection, better customer incentive timing, and future extensions such as TiDB Cloud integration and managed Flink stream processing, all without adding operational downtime.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Acts as Mercari's managed CDC and event-streaming backbone for product and service data.

solution_components.name: BigQuery
solution_components.role: Stores streamed business and customer data for analytics and downstream marketing use cases.

solution_components.name: Schema Registry
solution_components.role: Helps Mercari build and operate CDC infrastructure with governed event contracts.

data_flow: Database changes from Mercari's in-house microservices stream into Confluent Cloud, where CDC pipelines deliver the events to BigQuery and downstream fraud detection and marketing systems so teams can act on new customer and transaction data immediately.
business_outcome: Mercari accelerated fraud detection, eliminated missed timing for customer incentives, avoided Kafka outages, and reduced the engineering effort required to build and operate CDC pipelines at scale.
architecture_clues: Mercari's product teams run microservices on Kubernetes while the data platform team owns CDC infrastructure.
The team plans to expand the architecture with TiDB Cloud and managed Apache Flink.
Real-time CDC pipelines are shared across fraud, marketing, and analytics workflows.
